A discourse where the Buddha uses the simile of a boat to explain:
- The benefits of associating with good people (sappurisa)
- The dangers of associating with evil people (asappurisa)

[Vi+takka+ṇa]  CL=8 [From Nīti Dhātu 281, Itivuttaka Aṭṭhakathā 137, Abhidhamma Aṭṭhakathā 1.157, Paṭisambhidā Aṭṭhakathā 1.47,75, Vibhāvinī 90, Maṇimañjū 1.237]
The term vitakka is explained as:
['Vitakkenti etena, sayaṃ vā vitakketi, vitakkanaṃ mattamevāti vitakko'] - That by which one thinks, or that which thinks by itself, or that which is mere thinking.
['Vitakketīti vitakko, vitakkanaṃ vā vitakko'] - That which thinks is vitakka, or the act of thinking is vitakka.
['Ārammaṇaṃ vitakketi sampayutta-dhamma abhiniropetīti vitakko'] - That which directs associated mental states towards an object is vitakka.
The meanings are:
1. Vitakka:
a) The mental factor that causes thinking about an object
b) The mental factor that thinks about an object
c) The mental factor that is mere thinking
d) The mental factor that directs associated mental states towards an object
e) The decisive factor (vibhakka)
2. Vitakka and Vicāra (initial and sustained application)
3. Three Vitakka Suttas (refer to original sources)
Alternative forms: vitaka (Sanskrit), viakka (Prākrit), viyakka (Ardhamāgadhī)

Yatrakāmāvasāya(Pu)vīlyaṃ.] Super natural power which  can be fulfilled as per your desires in all wants/things (such as flying in the sky).
yavakhādana: [Yā+khādana] (na) CL=7 One who is eating Barley rice(alms).
yāgutaṇḍula: [Yāgu+taṇḍula] (na) CL=7 [Yāguyāattāya taṇḍulā yāgutaṇḍulā. Rū. 195.] The rice which is to boil for getting the rice porridge.
yāvacarimālopappahonaka: [Yāvacarimālopa+pahonaka] (ti) CL=7 Enough to eat until the final mouthful of alms.
yebhuyyasikākamma: [Yebhuyyasikā+kamma] (na) CL=7 Yebhuyya sika kamma, Yebhuyyasika Vinaya Kamma, Kamma which is follwing and making to many persons of moral rectitude.
yogakkhema: [Yoga+khema] (pu) CL=7 [Yoga-kkhema-saṃ. Yogakkhema-prā] (1) It is cessation of four Yogas ( Yoga mean shoulder yoke :lust yoke, life yoke, doctrine yoke and Ignorance yoke), Cessation of  Yoga, Can not ill-treated by four Yoga, Not compared with Yoga. (A) Arahattaphiula (fruition of the fourth and final stage in the Noble Eightfold Path), Nibbāna. (B) Nibbāna. (C) Arahattaphiula (fruition of the fourth and final stage in the Noble Eightfold Path). (D) Wealth/Sake. (2) Cessation of danger of four Yogas, Cessation of four Yogas. (3) Kāyacittasukha = Peace and tranquil of body and mind. (4) Without danger, Without harm.
yottaka: [Yottaka+] (na) CL=7 (1) A rope, Rope used in tug-of-war. (2) (iron) file. (holding one edge iron tools  and  brush things (such as knife which is the equipment of craft of blacksmithing ,Saṃkiuka. Sya).  See orignal.
yuttabalibadda: [Yutta+balibadda] (pu) CL=7 (Leading bull of a herd) , Chief bull is put (on the  vechicle for driving such as a coach or a cart).
yuttapamāṇajānana: [Yuttapamāṇa+jānana] (na) CL=7 Knowing about the proper case/status which is not sin. Knowing about proper extent.
yuttatara: [Yutta+tara] (ti) CL=7 [Yuttatara-saṃ.] It is more reasonable (or) Especially it is right (or) Especially it is in accordance with rules.
